_comment: Single source of truth for `muat reproduce`. experiments.md is generated/kept in sync with this file. URLs and sha256 values marked TODO must be filled once the Zenodo release exists.
_matrix_note: Group D is a 2x2 reproducibility matrix (train/inference x same/different environment) plus an hg38 pair. EVERY tag uses seed 1337 on purpose: to attribute a difference to the ENVIRONMENT, the seed must be held fixed, otherwise seed and environment are confounded. Expected outcomes differ by comparison: WITHIN one environment (the 10 repeats of any single tag) outputs must be BIT-IDENTICAL; ACROSS environments (d1 vs d2, d3 vs d4) they will NOT be bit-identical, because GPU and CPU use different kernels and reduction orders - the claim there is agreement within a stated tolerance, not bit-equality. Fix that tolerance before running so a normal float difference is not read as a failure.

d1.purpose: Training-run reproducibility, SAME environment (CSC Puhti GPU / bioconda). Input type SNV+MNV+pos+ges on the 80:20 pcawg_orig partition (train 1449 / test 363); trained 10x under the same seed. Expected: all 10 repeats BIT-IDENTICAL. Reported metrics come from the BEST epoch (best_val_first_logits.tsv), and the published checkpoint is the matching best_ckpt.pthx. Produces ckpt1, which d3 and d4 load.
d1._split_note: The 'val' key is the mechanical name the training code expects; semantically these 363 samples are the TEST set. 'Best epoch' is the epoch scoring highest on these same 363 (trainer.py:324), so the test set informed epoch selection - report it as a best-epoch figure. Publish best_ckpt.pthx (NOT model.pthx, which is the final epoch) as the d1_checkpoint asset, so the inference tags reproduce exactly the reported numbers.
d1._result_note: DONE 2026-08-07 (10/10 repeats). Best epoch 73. top1 0.851240 / top3 0.953168 / top5 0.986226 / weighted precision 0.860142 / weighted recall 0.851240 / weighted F1 0.847808 / macro F1 0.786709. sd = 0.000000 across all 10; logits, predictions AND the full 100-epoch evaluation.tsv curve are byte-identical. NOTE this run's environment label needs independent verification before being published as the Puhti/bioconda row.
d1.label: ckpt1

d1_snvmnvindelsv.purpose: Same cohort/split/hyperparameters/seed as d1, but trained on SNV+MNV+indel+SV instead of d1's SNV+MNV-only -- d1's own bundle has zero indel/SV/MEI data (verified), so this is a NEW tag with real richer data, not a modification of d1. No MEI: no such data exists for this cohort (checked -- BEDPE svclass values are only DEL/DUP/TRA/INV variants, and no separate MEI/retrotransposon callset exists). Neg deliberately left out (a separate synthetic-sampling design, not derived from real variant files -- may be added as its own tag later).
d1_snvmnvindelsv._data_note: SNV+MNV+indel are real PCAWG consensus calls (data/PCAWG/consensus_snv_indel/.../{snv_mnv,indel}). SV is synthesized from the consensus BEDPE files (data/PCAWG/consensus_sv/icgc/open) via muat/pkg_reproduce/make_snvmnvindelsv_vcfs.py -- each BEDPE row becomes two synthetic VCF SV-breakend records (one per breakpoint side), which the EXISTING, UNMODIFIED VCFReader already parses via its SVCLASS INFO tag (no muat code was changed). Tokenized with the shipped default dictionaries (NOT rebuilt) -- coverage verified: position/ges 100% mapped, motif 99.99% mapped (1300/21,678,396 rows, novel indel-context motifs).
d1_snvmnvindelsv._split_note: Reuses d1's own class_name/class_index directly (NOT re-derived from the PCAWG histology file, which disagrees with d1's labels on 7 samples -- a pre-existing minor metadata inconsistency, not fixed here). Split is d1's own 1449/363 partition minus the 18 samples (15 train + 3 val) with no SV data -- see make_d1_snvmnvindelsv_split.py.
d1_snvmnvindelsv.label: ckpt1
d1_snvmnvindelsv.environment: CSC Puhti GPU bioconda (same as d1 -- muat-d1c26)

d2_snvmnvindelsv.purpose: Same as d1_snvmnvindelsv (SNV+MNV+indel+SV, same cohort/split/hyperparameters/seed), DIFFERENT environment (CPU / custom-built container) -- mirrors how d2 relates to d1. Identical data_bundle/splits to d1_snvmnvindelsv; only device+install-mechanism differ.
d2_snvmnvindelsv.label: ckpt2_snvmnvindelsv
d2_snvmnvindelsv.environment: CSC Puhti CPU docker (custom-built image, matching d2's own switch away from BioContainers -- see run_reproduce_d2_x10.sbatch)

d3_snvmnvindelsv.purpose: Inference-run reproducibility for d1_snvmnvindelsv, SAME environment (GPU / bioconda-stack). Loads d1_snvmnvindelsv's checkpoint and predicts the snvmnvindelsv val split 10x under seed 1337. Mirrors d3's relationship to d1.
d3_snvmnvindelsv.environment: CSC Puhti GPU bioconda (same as d1_snvmnvindelsv -- muat-d1c26)

d4_snvmnvindelsv.purpose: Inference-run reproducibility for d1_snvmnvindelsv, DIFFERENT environment (CPU / custom-built container). Same checkpoint, same seed, same split as d3_snvmnvindelsv; only the environment differs. Mirrors d4's relationship to d1/d3.
d4_snvmnvindelsv.environment: CSC Puhti CPU docker (custom-built image, same as d2_snvmnvindelsv)

d7_snvmnvindelsv.purpose: Cross-OS/cross-architecture portability check for d1_snvmnvindelsv, answering R1-major-2/R2-5 (systematic reproducibility/portability evaluation across different computational architectures and operating environments -- every other tag in this matrix runs on the same HPC cluster, varying only device/install-method). Same checkpoint (d1_run1.pthx from ckpt1.zip) and same 360-sample val split as d3_snvmnvindelsv/d4_snvmnvindelsv, but executed on a genuinely different machine: a personal macOS laptop (Apple M4 Pro) via Docker, image built/run as linux/amd64 (Rosetta2/QEMU-emulated), NOT the cluster.
d7_snvmnvindelsv._not_via_reproduce_note: NOT runnable through `muat reproduce` or on this cluster at all -- must be run on the target machine directly with `docker build`/`docker run` (see run_d7_mac.sh, kept outside the repo since it references a local, machine-specific transfer layout). This entry documents the recipe/decision in the same ledger as every other tag.
d7_snvmnvindelsv._result_note: RUN 2026-08-28. Single run (no --seed, no 10x repeat -- this checks cross-platform AGREEMENT, not repeat-run determinism), --platform linux/amd64. Result: top1 0.8611111111111112 (vs d3_snvmnvindelsv's 0.8638888888888889 on the same 360 samples) -- 359/360 samples agree exactly; the 1 divergent sample was already a near-tie on the cluster reference. Written to data/results_d_same/d7/. See d8_snvmnvindelsv for the arm64-native rerun of the SAME checkpoint on the SAME machine -- identical to this result (0/360 mismatches between d7 and d8), confirming the divergence traces to Apple Silicon vs. the cluster's x86_64 CPU, not the amd64-emulated-vs-native choice.
d7_snvmnvindelsv.environment: Personal macOS (Apple M4 Pro) via Docker, linux/amd64 image (Rosetta2/QEMU-emulated) -- NOT the CSC cluster

d8_snvmnvindelsv.purpose: Same portability check as d7_snvmnvindelsv, on the SAME macOS machine (Apple M4 Pro) and SAME checkpoint/split, but with the Docker image built/run NATIVELY as linux/arm64 instead of the emulated linux/amd64 -- isolates whether Rosetta2/QEMU emulation itself was a source of divergence, as distinct from the underlying Apple Silicon CPU.
d8_snvmnvindelsv._result_note: RUN 2026-08-28 (same session as d7_snvmnvindelsv, via `PLATFORM=linux/arm64 run_d7_mac.sh`). Result: IDENTICAL to d7_snvmnvindelsv -- 0/360 mismatches between the two Mac runs, every class probability matching to the file's full displayed precision; both differ from d3_snvmnvindelsv by the same 8/360 samples (top1 0.8611111111111112). Conclusion: emulated-vs-native makes no difference; the small divergence from the cluster is attributable specifically to Apple Silicon vs. x86_64 CPU silicon. Written to data/results_d_same/d8/. Two real bugs found+fixed getting this run to actually complete (see run_d7_mac.sh comments): (1) input_list.txt was generated with host-absolute paths, unreachable inside the container's /data mount -- caused deterministic 0-samples-tokenized failures, not a mount-timing flake as first suspected; (2) the 'Error decompressing hg19.fa.gz...exit status 2' message is cosmetic (gzip's 'trailing garbage ignored' warning, inherent to the official Sanger download, not corruption) -- muat/util.py's gunzip_file() already only prints on this, never raises.
d8_snvmnvindelsv.environment: Personal macOS (Apple M4 Pro) via Docker, linux/arm64 image (native) -- NOT the CSC cluster

d9_snvmnvindelsv.purpose: Same portability check as d7_snvmnvindelsv/d8_snvmnvindelsv, on Windows (via Docker Desktop / WSL2) instead of macOS -- a genuinely different OS (unlike d7/d8, which both run a Linux container regardless of amd64-vs-arm64), and typically Intel/AMD x86_64 hardware -- expected to land bit-identical to d3_snvmnvindelsv/d4_snvmnvindelsv given the d3-vs-d4 finding that OS alone (on the same CPU family) makes no difference.
d9_snvmnvindelsv._result_note: NOT YET RUN. Blocked on access to Windows hardware (none used yet this session). Same plan as d7_snvmnvindelsv otherwise: single run, --platform linux/amd64, compare against d3_snvmnvindelsv's known result. (Renumbered from d8 to d9 2026-08-28 when d8 was reassigned to the Mac arm64-native rerun.)
d9_snvmnvindelsv.environment: Windows via Docker Desktop/WSL2 -- NOT the CSC cluster

d2.purpose: Training-run reproducibility, DIFFERENT environment (CSC Puhti CPU / docker). Identical to d1 in every respect except the environment - same seed 1337, same split, same hyperparameters - so any difference is attributable to the environment alone. Trained 10x. Expected: the 10 repeats bit-identical WITHIN this environment; versus d1 (GPU) agreement within tolerance, NOT bit-equality. Produces ckpt2.
d2._comparison_note: d1 vs d2 changes device (GPU->CPU) AND install method (bioconda->docker) at once. If a discrepancy appears and needs attributing, add an intermediate run (Puhti GPU + docker) to separate the container from the device.
d2.label: ckpt2

d3.purpose: Inference-run reproducibility, SAME environment (CSC Puhti GPU / bioconda). Loads ckpt1 and predicts the 363-sample test split 10x under seed 1337. Repeats are meaningful because inference subsamples mutations per sample. Expected: all 10 runs bit-identical (enforced by assert_identical).

d4.purpose: Inference-run reproducibility, DIFFERENT environment (CSC Puhti CPU / docker). Same ckpt1, same seed 1337, same 363-sample test split as d3; only the environment differs. Expected: the 10 runs bit-identical WITHIN this environment; versus d3 (GPU) agreement within tolerance, NOT bit-equality.

d5.purpose: Training on GRCh38. Same recipe as d1 (seed 1337, same 1449/363 sample partition, same hyperparameters) but on hg38-preprocessed inputs, isolating the effect of the genome build. Trained 10x. Produces ckpt3.
d5._hg38_note: NOT RUNNABLE YET - three things must be settled first. (1) BUILD DIRECTION: muat supports two hg38 paths and they are different experiments - reader.py:254 lifts hg38 input DOWN to hg19 and reuses the hg19 pipeline, whereas reader.py:284 hg38_native keeps hg38 coordinates and uses the GRCh38 genic/exonic tracks in pkg_data/genomic_tracks/h38. This recipe assumes hg38_native on hg19->hg38 lifted PCAWG data. (2) POSITION DICTIONARY: only one dictionary ships (muat/extfile/dictChpos.tsv, 2915 chrom_bin tokens) and it is hg19-derived; under hg38_native the coordinates are hg38 but the lookup is against hg19 bins. Verify whether it must be regenerated for hg38 - if so the vocabulary changes and ckpt3 is not comparable to ckpt1 token-for-token. (3) DATA: no hg38 bundle exists; all 1812 samples need re-preprocessing and a new Zenodo asset. This is a much larger job than d1-d4 combined.
d5.label: ckpt3
d5._splits_note: Reuses the hg19 split id-lists on purpose: the same 1449/363 aliquots, so d1 and d5 differ only in genome build. This works only if the hg38 bundle names its files with the same <uuid>.muat.tsv basenames.

d6.purpose: Inference on GRCh38. Loads ckpt3 (from d5) and predicts the hg38 363-sample test split 10x under seed 1337, same environment as d5. Expected: all 10 runs bit-identical.
d6._hg38_note: Blocked on d5 - see its _hg38_note. Depends on both the hg38 bundle and ckpt3 existing.

d5_pubhg38._not_via_reproduce_note: NOT runnable through `muat reproduce` -- this schema has no field for per-tag custom dictionaries, and this recipe needs its own (dictMutation_pubhg38.tsv / dictChpos_pubhg38.tsv / dictGES_pubhg38.tsv, not the shipped defaults). Run via run_reproduce_d5_pubhg38_x10.sbatch instead, which calls `muat train from-scratch` directly. This entry exists only so the recipe/decision is documented in the same ledger as every other tag.
d5_pubhg38.purpose: REPLACES the old (never-runnable) d5 idea of training on hg38-native PCAWG (see d5's own _hg38_note - that data was never re-preprocessed and would have been a much larger job than d1-d4 combined). Reuses the already-working public GDC hg38 demo cohort instead: 6 TCGA WES cancer types, 590 samples, native hg38, SNV+motif+position+ges. Same seed 1337, trained 10x. Produces the checkpoint d6_pubhg38 loads.
d5_pubhg38._result_note: A single (unseeded-in-practice-but-default-1337) run of this exact recipe already completed once, BEFORE the mutation-sampling-determinism fix (v0.1.26) existed: data/hg38_public_demo/model/best_ckpt.pthx, val top1 0.7753 / test top1 0.7386. Left untouched as a historical reference; d5_pubhg38's 10 repeats write to fresh data/reproduce_results/d5_pubhg38_repNN_<jobid>/ dirs and re-train with the fixed code.
d5_pubhg38.label: ckpt_pubhg38
d5_pubhg38.environment: CSC Puhti GPU bioconda (muat-d1c26, same as d1/d3)

d6_pubhg38._not_via_reproduce_note: NOT runnable through `muat reproduce`, for the same reason as d5_pubhg38. Run via run_reproduce_d6_pubhg38.sbatch, which calls `muat predict from-checkpoint --seed 1337` directly in a 10x bash loop. --seed on `predict` was added to the repo specifically to make this check possible and is NOT in the installed muat-d1c26 (v0.1.26) -- the script runs against repo source via PYTHONPATH, not the installed package.
d6_pubhg38.purpose: Inference-run reproducibility for d5_pubhg38: loads its checkpoint and predicts the 89-sample public-hg38 validation set 10x under seed 1337, same environment as d5_pubhg38. Expected: all 10 runs bit-identical. d5/d6 use only the train and validation cohorts; the held-out test split is not used anywhere in this reproducibility experiment.
d6_pubhg38.environment: CSC Puhti GPU bioconda (muat-d1c26, same as d5_pubhg38)

a1_d1.purpose: Training-run reproducibility on REAL PCAWG controlled-access data (the a1 scenario in the abc reproducibility matrix), SAME environment as d1_snvmnvindelsv (GPU / bioconda). Full mutation-type recipe (SNV+MNV+indel+SV/MEI+Neg), same architecture/hyperparameters/seed as d1_snvmnvindelsv, on a DIFFERENT, controlled-access cohort (2585 samples, 24 tumour types) built directly from the original MuAt paper's own per-sample tokenized training data (litePCAWG), not reconstructed. Trained 3x under the same seed. Expected: all 3 repeats bit-identical WITHIN this environment (same claim as d1/d1_snvmnvindelsv, at 3 repeats instead of 10 -- see _repeat_note).
a1_d1._access_note: CONTROLLED-ACCESS BY DESIGN, not merely 'not yet published' -- this cohort derives from ICGC PCAWG's DACO-gated somatic mutation calls (data/PCAWG2019/PCAWG.somatic_SISM.*.tsv). It will never have a public download URL; a legitimate reproducer must obtain their own DACO access to the same donor IDs (Supplementary Table S9) and run this repo's preprocessing code themselves, or point --cache-dir at their own DACO-cleared copy. Do not fill in a url for the a1_litepcawg_preprocessed asset below.
a1_d1._repeat_note: 3 repeats, not d1_snvmnvindelsv's 10 -- a deliberately smaller determinism check (same claim, lower compute cost), agreed with the user 2026-09-07. Still sufficient to detect non-determinism: any repeat-to-repeat difference at all falsifies bit-identical reproducibility, regardless of repeat count.
a1_d1.label: a1_ckpt1
a1_d1.environment: CSC Puhti GPU bioconda (same as d1_snvmnvindelsv -- muat-d1c26)

a1_d1_hfmatch.purpose: Architecture-matched ablation of a1_d1: reproduces the ORIGINALLY PUBLISHED HuggingFace benchmark_wgs.zip checkpoint's architecture+sampling config for mutation_type snv+mnv+indel+svmei (motif-only model -- use_position/use_ges both False, matching that checkpoint's model_name=MuAtMotif -- with n_layer=1/n_head=1/n_emb=512, matching that checkpoint's model_config.json exactly; mutation_type_ratio {snv:0.3,mnv:0.4,indel:0.2,sv_mei:0.2,neg:0} comes automatically from mutation_type via get_mut_ratio() and matches that checkpoint's own pickled ratio too), trained on the SAME a1 controlled-access cohort/split as a1_d1, but with the FULL 2587-sample cohort (see _2587_note) rather than a1_d1's 2585. Purpose: test whether a1_d1's accuracy gap vs a0 (0.803 vs 0.869 on the matched held-out fold) is explained by a1_d1's motif+position+GES architecture rather than a data or pipeline defect.
a1_d1_hfmatch._hyperparam_note: The original checkpoint's own trainer_config.json is EMPTY (no learning_rate/batch_size/epoch/seed recorded, confirmed by inspecting benchmark_wgs_ckpt/snv+mnv+indel+svmei/fold1.pthx directly) -- only model_config.json (architecture) and dataloader_config.json (sampling) fields could be matched. Optimizer hyperparameters below are inherited unchanged from a1_d1 since there is nothing else to match against.
a1_d1_hfmatch._2587_note: a1_d1's splits/a1_{train,val}.tsv total only 2585 (litePCAWG has zero mutation data for 2 real-labeled samples: f848b66f-bd9e-4fba-afd4-eb58848d1ef4 and a876398c-5b1d-444f-a360-5fe2db697480, both Breast-AdenoCA -- confirmed a0's own published-checkpoint evaluation is bounded to 2585 too, same gap, not an a1-specific shortfall). User asked for the full nominal 2587 anyway: both samples' fold assignment (trainfullpcawg.csv/valfullpcawg.csv) places them in fold1's TRAIN set (never fold1's val), so they were backfilled from the 'ours' from-scratch PCAWG2019-reconstruction pipeline (data/pcawg_trainvalsplit/tokenized/, already built, non-fatal minor row loss from a few duplicate-position SV rows on one sample) into a NEW splits/a1_train_full.tsv (a1_train.tsv + these 2 rows, class_index 1 matching Breast-AdenoCA's existing index, renamed from an earlier a1_train_2587.tsv to avoid colliding with a1_train.tsv's different 2326-sample content) and copied into litepcawg_tokenized/ so the bundle now has all 2587 files. val is UNCHANGED (both samples are fold1-train-only, so a1_val.tsv's 259 held-out samples, and the a0-vs-a1 fold1 comparison, are unaffected). a1_d1 itself was deliberately left untouched (still 2585, already packaged) -- this backfill applies only to this tag.
a1_d1_hfmatch.label: a1_ckpt_hfmatch
a1_d1_hfmatch.environment: CSC Puhti GPU bioconda (same as a1_d1 -- muat-d1c26)

a1_d2.purpose: Same as a1_d1 (SNV+MNV+indel+SV/MEI+Neg, same controlled-access cohort/split/hyperparameters/seed), DIFFERENT environment (CPU / custom-built container) -- mirrors how d2_snvmnvindelsv relates to d1_snvmnvindelsv. Identical data_bundle/splits to a1_d1; only device+install-mechanism differ.
a1_d2.label: a1_ckpt2
a1_d2.environment: CSC Puhti CPU docker (custom-built image, same as d2_snvmnvindelsv)

a1_d3.purpose: Inference-run reproducibility for a1_d1, SAME environment (GPU / bioconda-stack). Loads a1_d1's checkpoint and predicts the a1 val split 3x under seed 1337. Mirrors d3_snvmnvindelsv's relationship to d1_snvmnvindelsv.
a1_d3.environment: CSC Puhti GPU bioconda (same as a1_d1 -- muat-d1c26)

a1_d4.purpose: Inference-run reproducibility for a1_d1, DIFFERENT environment (CPU / custom-built container). Same checkpoint, same seed, same split as a1_d3; only the environment differs. Mirrors d4_snvmnvindelsv's relationship to d1_snvmnvindelsv/d3_snvmnvindelsv.
a1_d4.environment: CSC Puhti CPU docker (custom-built image, same as d2_snvmnvindelsv/a1_d2)

b1.purpose: GEL SPE inference-portability check ('Inference on GEL full set using a1, no fine-tune' from the original a/b/c matrix sketch): predict using BOTH a0's original published fold1 checkpoint (mutation_type snv+mnv+indel+svmei) AND a1_d1_hfmatch's freshly-trained checkpoint (same mutation_type, motif-only architecture matching the published checkpoint) against litePCAWG's SAME 259-sample val split (muat/pkg_reproduce/splits/a1_val.tsv), but executed INSIDE the Genomics England secure processing environment (SPE) instead of the CSC cluster, 3x per checkpoint (--seed 1337 each time) to check inference determinism inside GEL itself, not just agreement with the CSC-cluster reference. a0's fold1 checkpoint's reference is a0's own CSC-cluster fold1 result (CPU/bioconda, snv+mnv+indel+svmei); a1_d1_hfmatch's reference is its own GPU/bioconda training-time evaluation on the CSC cluster (no CPU/container twin exists for a1_d1_hfmatch, unlike a1_d1/a3/a4). Same relationship as d7/d8 (Mac) to d3/d4 (cluster): a cross-environment AGREEMENT check, this time also carrying its own internal repeat-run determinism check.
b1._scope_note: b2 (fine-tune on GEL starting from a1) and b3 (inference/test on GEL using b2's fine-tuned checkpoint) remain explicitly OUT OF SCOPE -- real data-governance/DACO complexity, would duplicate the original MuAt2 paper's own PCAWG-vs-GEL comparison, and require a new unreviewed statistic cleared through Airlock for no added portability evidence beyond what b1 already delivers. b1 only ever loads existing, already-trained checkpoints -- no training happens inside GEL.
b1._not_via_reproduce_note: NOT runnable through `muat reproduce` or on this cluster at all -- must be run inside the GEL SPE directly, using data/b1_gel_portability/run_b1_gel.sh (kept outside the tags' normal cache-dir/asset flow, same reason as run_d7_mac.sh: the target environment's paths/layout are machine-specific, not something a shared recipe can resolve). Uses GEL's REAL container workflow (fetched from https://re-docs.genomicsengland.co.uk/hpc_containers/ 2026-09-07, already cited but never exercised in si_revision.tex's 'Using muat via a container' section): Singularity, pulling a custom-pushed dependency-stack image via GEL's Artifactory proxy. Runs muat from REPO SOURCE via PYTHONPATH inside that container (bind-mounting a copy of this repo at the same commit both checkpoints' predict jobs ran from), exactly like a1_d2/d2_snvmnvindelsv already do on the cluster -- NOT the official quay.io/biocontainers/muat image directly, since a1_d1_hfmatch runs at muat.__version__ 0.1.28, not yet released to bioconda/BioContainers (the released d1-d9 experiments are pinned to v0.1.27). This means no new muat release is required before running b1 -- only the dependency stack (python/pytorch/numpy/pandas/scikit-learn, already built+verified as muat-env-cpu-v0.1.26.yml / data/containers/muat_0.1.26_cpu.sif's source image) needs pushing to a registry GEL's Artifactory can reach. This entry documents the recipe/decision in the same ledger as every other tag.
b1._safety_note: Only prediction files (PCAWG sample UUID + predicted class + logits) are exported from the SPE via GEL's named egress process, Airlock -- litePCAWG is PCAWG controlled-access data GEL already holds a copy of (from the original MuAt2 study's combined PCAWG+GEL pretraining), NOT GEL patient data, so nothing about any GEL patient is computed or exported. Still requires an actual Airlock request before export, as a formality -- see run_b1_gel.sh's header.
b1._result_note: DONE 2026-09-09 (image quay.io/primasanjaya/muat-cpu-deps:0.1.26-b2, run_b1_gel_selfdata.sh -- see _selfdata_note for the data-provenance decision behind this specific image). Both checkpoints deterministic across all 3 GEL repeats (sd=0.000000), n=259 both sides. Reported result: a0_fold1 0.845560 (cluster ref 0.861004, delta -0.015444, ~4/259 samples), a1_d1_hfmatch 0.806950 (cluster ref 0.814672, delta -0.007722, ~2/259 samples). Both gaps are confirmed NOT a data/provenance artifact (see _selfdata_note) -- something about the GEL runtime/environment itself (e.g. a different torch/BLAS/numpy build than whatever produced the CSC-cluster reference) not yet isolated further. Next step (not yet done): a per-sample compare_environments.py diff on the Airlocked-out result_selfdata/ against the same cluster references, to check whether the disagreeing samples are near-ties (floating-point/library-version noise, a legitimate portability nuance) or genuine flips (a real defect) -- aggregate accuracy alone can't distinguish these.
b1._selfdata_note: Runs against quay.io/primasanjaya/muat-cpu-deps:0.1.26-b2 (run_b1_gel_selfdata.sh), which bakes the exact 259 CSC-cluster litepcawg_tokenized files (data/b1_gel_portability/litepcawg_val_data/) directly into the image, rather than relying on GEL's own separately-imported litePCAWG copy + in-SPE merge (an earlier internal validation image, 0.1.26-b1/run_b1_gel.sh, was used only to check whether GEL's own copy/merge reconstruction explained an observed a0_fold1 gap -- it did not: a0_fold1's accuracy was identical either way -- and is not itself part of the reported result). User's explicit call 2026-09-09: extends the checkpoints' 'software artifact, not raw data' override (see _not_via_reproduce_note and Dockerfile.b1's header) to this merged/tokenized val-set bundle too -- a stronger instance of that override than the checkpoints were, since it is actual tokenized mutation calls rather than model weights. The image tag itself is deliberately plain/numeric (0.1.26-b2, not a descriptive name) since it is public on quay.io. The PCAWG-side DACO notification gap from the original CSC->GEL litePCAWG transfer (see the assistant's memory of this project) remains separately unresolved.
b1.environment: Genomics England secure processing environment (SPE) -- NOT the CSC cluster

a1_litepcawg_preprocessed.description: Preprocessed controlled-access a1 cohort (2585 samples, 24 tumour types), built DIRECTLY from litePCAWG (gitlab.com/primasanjaya/litepcawg -- the original MuAt paper's own real per-sample tokenized training data), not reconstructed from raw PCAWG2019 files. Backs a1_d1/a1_d2/a1_d3/a1_d4. See make_a1_litepcawg_tokenized.py for the build process and Supplementary Table S9 for the sample list (donor ID, aliquot ID, histology, fold).
a1_litepcawg_preprocessed._access_note: NEVER will have a url -- this asset is controlled-access by design (see a1_d1's _access_note in the tags section), not merely undeposited. A legitimate reproducer obtains their own DACO access and either runs this repo's preprocessing code themselves against the same donor IDs (Supplementary Table S9), or requests a controlled-access-compliant copy through the appropriate DACO channel. This entry's extract_subdir is populated by a plain symlink to data/pcawg_trainvalsplit/litepcawg_tokenized (see run_reproduce_a1_d1_x03.sbatch's PREREQUISITE), NOT by `muat fetch` extracting an actual archive -- there is nothing to fetch.

a1_d1_checkpoint.description: LOCAL-ONLY, controlled-access-derived, not published/fetchable. Checkpoint produced by experiment a1_d1 (SNV+MNV+indel+SV/MEI+Neg on the controlled-access a1 cohort). BEST-EPOCH checkpoint: rename a1_d1_rep01_<arrayid>/best_ckpt.pthx to a1_d1.pthx and stage at cache_dir/assets/.

a1_d2_checkpoint.description: LOCAL-ONLY, controlled-access-derived, not published/fetchable. Checkpoint produced by experiment a1_d2 (same recipe/seed as a1_d1, CPU/container environment). Cross-environment evidence only, same role as d2_snvmnvindelsv_checkpoint.

a1_d1_hfmatch_checkpoint.description: LOCAL-ONLY, controlled-access-derived, not published/fetchable. Checkpoint produced by experiment a1_d1_hfmatch (architecture-matched ablation of a1_d1: motif-only, matching the originally published benchmark_wgs.zip checkpoint's architecture). BEST-EPOCH checkpoint: rename a1_d1_hfmatch_rep01_<arrayid>/best_ckpt.pthx to a1_d1_hfmatch.pthx and stage at cache_dir/assets/.

a1_d1_hfmatch_all_repeats.description: a1_ckpt_hfmatch.zip - all 3 best-epoch checkpoints from the 3 repeats of a1_d1_hfmatch (GPU/bioconda, PCAWG controlled-access cohort, motif-only architecture matched to the original published benchmark_wgs.zip configuration), plus MANIFEST.tsv and README.md. Trained model weights only, no controlled-access mutation/genomic data. Determinism evidence for the manuscript (all 3 repeats bit-identical). Members named a1_ckpt_hfmatch_rep01.pthx..a1_ckpt_hfmatch_rep03.pthx.

d1_snvmnvindelsv_checkpoint.description: LOCAL-ONLY, not published/fetchable. Checkpoint produced by experiment d1_snvmnvindelsv (SNV+MNV+indel+SV). BEST-EPOCH checkpoint: rename d1_snvmnvindelsv_rep01_<arrayid>/best_ckpt.pthx to d1_snvmnvindelsv.pthx and stage at cache_dir/assets/.

d2_snvmnvindelsv_checkpoint.description: LOCAL-ONLY, not published/fetchable. Checkpoint produced by experiment d2_snvmnvindelsv (same recipe/seed as d1_snvmnvindelsv, CPU/container environment). Published as cross-environment evidence only, same role as d2_checkpoint.

d1_snvmnvindelsv_all_repeats.description: ckpt1.zip - all 10 best-epoch checkpoints from the 10 repeats of d1_snvmnvindelsv (GPU/bioconda, SNV+MNV+indel+SV), plus MANIFEST.tsv and README.md. Determinism evidence for the manuscript. Members named d1_run1.pthx..d1_run10.pthx.

d2_snvmnvindelsv_all_repeats.description: ckpt2.zip - all 10 best-epoch checkpoints from the 10 repeats of d2_snvmnvindelsv (CPU/container arm, Debian base host CentOS 7), plus MANIFEST.tsv and README.md. Determinism evidence for the manuscript. Members named d2_run1.pthx..d2_run10.pthx (matching ckpt1.zip's d1_run*.pthx convention for d1_snvmnvindelsv).

d5_pubhg38_checkpoint.description: LOCAL-ONLY, not published/fetchable yet. Checkpoint produced by experiment d5_pubhg38 (public GDC hg38-native training). BEST-EPOCH checkpoint (epoch 67): repeat 1's best_ckpt.pthx, copied verbatim by package_checkpoints.py.

d5_pubhg38_all_repeats.description: ckpt3.zip - all 10 best-epoch checkpoints from the 10 repeats of d5_pubhg38 (public GDC hg38-native training), plus MANIFEST.tsv and README.md. Determinism evidence for the manuscript. Members named d5_run1.pthx..d5_run10.pthx (matching ckpt1.zip's d1_run*.pthx convention for d1_snvmnvindelsv).

pubhg38_tcga_preprocessed.description: Preprocessed public GDC TCGA hg38-native samples backing d5_pubhg38/d6_pubhg38: one <sample>.muat.tsv per aliquot for the 502 train+validation samples (413 train / 89 val), plus the corpus-level dictionaries (dicts/) and the exact train_split.tsv/val_split.tsv used. Pins the exact cohort since the original cohort-selection step queries the live GDC API and is not itself byte-reproducible (see documentation/README_public_hg38.md). Deliberately excludes the held-out test split, matching pcawg_open_preprocessed's train+val-only convention.
pubhg38_tcga_preprocessed._sha256_note: Verified 2026-09-03 against data/reproduce_release/pubhg38_tcga_muat.tar.gz (2.0 MB, 502 samples). Archive is byte-reproducible: sorted file list, fixed mtime/ownership, gzip -n -9 (rebuild reproduces the identical sha256).

d1_checkpoint.description: Checkpoint produced by experiment d1 (PCAWG-open, snv+mnv+pos+ges). This is the BEST-EPOCH checkpoint: upload d1_rep01_<arrayid>/best_ckpt.pthx renamed to d1_canonical.pthx. Renamed 2026-08-24 from d1.pthx to free that name for the manuscript's newer, richer full-mutation-spectrum d1_snvmnvindelsv checkpoint, which the performance-report spreadsheet now reports as its 'd1' row.

d2_checkpoint.description: ckpt2 - checkpoint produced by experiment d2 (same recipe and seed as d1, trained in the CSC Puhti CPU / docker environment). Published as cross-environment evidence; no other tag loads it. Upload the BEST-EPOCH best_ckpt.pthx renamed to d2.pthx.

d5_checkpoint.description: ckpt3_canonical - checkpoint produced by experiment d5 (blocked PCAWG hg38-native training, see d5's own _hg38_note -- never built, does not exist). Renamed 2026-08-24 from d5.pthx/ckpt3.zip to free those names for d5_pubhg38's real checkpoint (the manuscript's 'd5' row) -- see d5_pubhg38_checkpoint.

assets._repeat_archive_note: The *_all_repeats archives below are EVIDENCE, not run-time dependencies: no tag references them, so 'muat fetch' never downloads them and a reproduce run does not need them. They are published so a reader can verify the determinism claim independently, by checking that the inner weight.pth of every repeat has the same sha256. Build them with muat/pkg_reproduce/package_checkpoints.py, which writes a byte-reproducible archive (fixed member timestamps) so the sha256 recorded here is itself reproducible.

d1_all_repeats.description: ckpt1_canonical.zip - all 10 best-epoch checkpoints from the 10 repeats of d1, plus MANIFEST.tsv (per-repeat sha256 of the container and of the inner weight.pth) and README.md. Determinism evidence for the manuscript. Renamed 2026-08-24 from ckpt1.zip -- see d1_checkpoint's note; 'ckpt1.zip' now refers to d1_snvmnvindelsv's archive instead.

d2_all_repeats.description: ckpt2_canonical.zip - all 10 best-epoch checkpoints from the 10 repeats of d2 (CPU / docker arm), same format as ckpt1_canonical.zip. Renamed 2026-09-03 from ckpt2.zip -- see d2_checkpoint's note; 'ckpt2.zip' now refers to d2_snvmnvindelsv's archive instead. This rename was missed during the 2026-08-24 d1/d5 renames (this exact mismatch -- a stale sha256 under the reused 'ckpt2.zip' name -- was caught and fixed by cross-checking against the real uploaded file).

d5_all_repeats.description: ckpt3_canonical.zip - all 10 best-epoch checkpoints from the 10 repeats of d5 (blocked PCAWG hg38-native training). Does not exist and never will -- see the _hg38_note on tag d5. Renamed 2026-08-24, see d5_checkpoint.

hg38.description: GRCh38/hg38 reference (UCSC goldenPath). Same URL muat/download.py:104 uses. Needed for hg38 preprocessing (tags d5/d6); note the `muat download` CLI only exposes --pcawg, so the reference is fetched via download_reference(), not the CLI.

pcawg_open_hg38_preprocessed.description: GRCh38 counterpart of pcawg_open_preprocessed: the same 1812 aliquots preprocessed against hg38, one <sample>.muat.tsv per aliquot, SAME basenames as the hg19 bundle so the shipped split id-lists resolve unchanged. DOES NOT EXIST YET - requires re-preprocessing all 1812 samples; see the _hg38_note on tag d5.

pcawg_full_mutations_preprocessed.description: Preprocessed SNV+MNV+indel+SV tokenized files (<sample>.muat.tsv) for the 1794-sample d1_snvmnvindelsv cohort (1,434 train / 360 val), built by merging real PCAWG consensus snv_mnv/indel VCFs with synthetic VCF records derived from the consensus SV BEDPE files (muat/pkg_reproduce/make_snvmnvindelsv_vcfs.py), then tokenized with the shipped default dictionaries (100% position/ges coverage, 99.99% motif coverage). No MEI data exists for this cohort. Backs d1_snvmnvindelsv/d2_snvmnvindelsv/d3_snvmnvindelsv/d4_snvmnvindelsv/d7-d9_snvmnvindelsv -- i.e. this is the bundle the manuscript's actual reported classification results (top-1 86.39%/85.83%) trace to, NOT pcawg_open_preprocessed.
pcawg_full_mutations_preprocessed._sha256_note: Verified 2026-09-03 against data/reproduce_release/pcawg_snvmnvindelsv_muat.tar.gz (237 MB, 1794 entries, sample IDs cross-checked exactly against splits/pcawg_orig_snvmnvindelsv_{train,val}.tsv). Byte-reproducible: sorted file list, fixed mtime/ownership, gzip -n -9 (rebuild reproduces the identical sha256).

pcawg_open_preprocessed.description: Preprocessed open-access PCAWG samples, one friendly <sample>.muat.tsv (plain TSV) per aliquot (1812 samples, 17 tumour types), built by make_bundle.py from the internal *.token.gc.genic.exonic.cs.tsv.gz files. Backs ONLY the superseded plain d1/d2/d3/d4 tags (their checkpoints were never published either) -- the manuscript's actual reported d1-d4 results are d1_snvmnvindelsv etc., which use pcawg_full_mutations_preprocessed instead. Deliberately NOT on Zenodo: publishing it alongside ckpt1.zip/ckpt2.zip (which need the 1794-sample bundle) would mislead readers into pairing the wrong data with those checkpoints.
pcawg_open_preprocessed._sha256_note: Value kept for provenance only (matches data/reproduce_release/pcawg_open_muat.tar.gz on disk, 222 MB, 1812 entries) -- this file was REMOVED from the Zenodo record 2026-09-03, do not re-fill url.

pcawg_open_raw.description: Raw open-access PCAWG consensus mutations from ICGC object storage (only fetched with --from-raw).
